observations: Torah #200 has zero bechina edges in torahData.js, and the source text contains no bechina language. The teaching presents exactly one relationship: fulfilling the Torah from poverty (קיום התורה מעוני) produces the merit to ultimately fulfill it from wealth (זכות לקיים מעושר), with gilgul (reincarnation) explaining how this promise bridges across lifetimes. This is a pure eitza relationship — sequential cause-and-effect, directional — not a bechina equivalence of shared essential nature. The framework requires bechina-connected concepts to form a package. Since there are no bechina relationships in this Torah at all, and all core concepts (poverty-observance, wealth-observance, gilgul, earlier tzaddikim, contemporary tzaddikim) are causally or contextually related rather than essentially equivalent, no package can be proposed — not even with the minimum size of two nodes. If these five concepts were added to the dataset, the correct edge type would be eitza (or contextual/definitional), not bechina. They would form a causal chain, not a conceptual cluster of parallel aspects. There is no candidate cluster of concepts sharing a common essential nature in this teaching, and therefore no new packages can be proposed.
